elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall ...", so all three limbs are triggered by either expiry or termination, and by termination for any reason (including termination on the 90-day notice in 4.1).

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — six-month duration at the Customer's election, matching the preferred position.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) ends "at HDI's then-current rates", tracking the playbook's model language (no uplift cap is required at the preferred level).

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return all Content, user information and transaction data of the Company" — the 30-day clock is expressly anchored to the expiry/termination event, not left to an undefined trigger.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return "in a commonly used, machine-readable format", which is the playbook's own formulation of a standard machine-readable format.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "thereafter delete such Content, information and data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company" — deletion is sequenced after return ("thereafter"), so the walk-away risk of immediate deletion on termination is avoided.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same trigger language: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "up to six (6) months" of assistance at the Company's request necessarily makes at least 90 days of assistance available, exceeding the fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of the Company's Content, user information and transaction data "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination" in a commonly used, machine-readable format.

reasons: Finding kind is correctly characterised as missing: Section 4.1-4.2(c) deal only with term, 90-day notice and the Termination Payment; Sections 1.4/1.5 access rights are expressly limited to the term; and no other clause requires return of the Company's Content, user information or transaction data on exit. The insertion is therefore the right remedy rather than a re-draft.

Preferred checklist is complete in operative language — six months of assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion sequenced after return. The fallback is offered only in the comment, which is appropriate because the operative text sits at the preferred level and independently satisfies the fallback floor.

Minimal: a single concise insertion in the termination section; no existing favourable language is deleted or duplicated, and no extra requirements (free assistance, rate caps, escrow, penalties) are added beyond the checklist.

Preserves intent: the 4.1 renewal/notice mechanic, the 4.2 Termination Payment and its eight quarterly instalments, and the 10.7 survival period are all left untouched and are not contradicted by the new obligations.

Drafting repair (non-blocking, not an element failure): the rendered clause carries no section number even though the rationale and comment call it "Section 4.3" — number it 4.3 in the instrument so the cross-references in the comment are accurate.

Residual risk worth closing (non-blocking): Section 10.7 enumerates only Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 as surviving, and the new clause is not listed. The obligations are by their nature post-termination and 4.2(c) already contemplates performance after the Termination Date, so the insertion is not internally inconsistent; but a one-word conforming change adding "4.3" to the 10.7 list (or the words "and Section 4.3") would remove any expressio unius argument that HDI's exit obligations lapse on termination.

Confirm on the next pass that the defined term "Content" as used in the Agreement captures all Company-supplied material; the clause is qualified "of the Company", which is the correct customer-side scoping, but a residual data category (e.g. logs or back-ups held by HDI) should be swept in if Section 8.1's scope proves narrower.
